internal.title: Incident Report: Elevated Error Rate in Checkout Service Due to Payment Service Flag Misconfiguration
internal.body:
At 12:13 UTC on 2026-11-08, an alert was triggered for a high error rate in the checkout service. Initial diagnosis identified the root cause as an error injection in the payment service related to an increased failure flag setting (paymentFailure flag set to 10%). This flag change caused invalid token errors, leading to elevated error rates downstream in the checkout service.

The issue was detected and diagnosed by 12:33 UTC. A mitigation action was proposed and approved to disable the problematic flag. The flag was disabled at 12:33:15 UTC, resulting in a rapid recovery of the service error rate to normal levels.

No deployment issues were found. The incident was resolved by disabling the paymentFailure flag, which restored normal service operation. Monitoring confirmed stable error rates post-recovery.

Timeline:
- 12:13:18 UTC: Alert received for high error rate in checkout
- 12:33:08 UTC: Diagnosis identified payment service error injection due to flag
- 12:33:14 UTC: Proposed disabling paymentFailure flag
- 12:33:15 UTC: Flag disabled and recovery verified

Action items include reviewing flag change approval processes to prevent similar incidents.
